issues.legal_issue: A testamentary life interest given to a Hindu wife for her maintenance enlarges into an absolute interest when it recognizes her pre-existing maintenance right and she possesses or enjoys the property.
material_facts: The owner’s will gave his wife lifetime enjoyment of specified property and provided for her use of related facilities.
The wife had a pre-existing right to maintenance from her husband’s property and continued to enjoy the property during her lifetime.
The will’s arrangement was not disputed, and the property was treated as having been given to the wife for her maintenance.
The trial court treated the wife’s interest as limited and recognized a vested remainder in another family member; the High Court held that the wife acquired absolute ownership.
issues.conclusion: The wife’s limited interest enlarged into an absolute interest; the remainder was extinguished, and she could bequeath the property. The High Court’s decision was correct and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is construed liberally to enlarge a Hindu woman’s limited interest where the property is held under a pre-existing right, including a right to maintenance. Section 14(2) applies to a grant creating a new and independent title for the first time, not to an instrument recognizing a pre-existing right. No express statement that a life interest is granted in lieu of maintenance is necessary where that purpose is established by the circumstances. This follows V. Tulasamma v. Sesha Reddy (1977) 3 SCC 99, R.B. S.S. Munnalal v. S.S. Rajkumar, AIR 1962 SC 1493, Nirmal Chand v. Vidya Wanti (1969) 3 SCC 628, Thota Sesharathamma v. Thota Manikyamma (1991) 4 SCC 312, Shakuntala Devi v. Kamla (2005) 5 SCC 390, and Nazar Singh v. Jagjit Kaur (1996) 1 SCC 35. Mst. Karmi v. Amru (1972) 4 SCC 86 did not govern these facts; Sadhu Singh v. Gurdwara Sahib Narike (2006) 8 SCC 75 was distinguishable because it proceeded on the basis that no pre-existing right existed. Section 30’s recognition of testamentary disposition does not displace the operation of Section 14(1) in these circumstances.

rule.if: testamentary_property_dispute and spouse_preexisting_maintenance_right and property_given_for_lifetime_enjoyment and maintenance_purpose_apparent and continuous_possession

predicates.testamentary_property_dispute: The dispute concerns ownership of property under or following a testamentary disposition.
predicates.spouse_preexisting_maintenance_right: The recipient spouse had a pre-existing right to maintenance from the property-owning spouse or that spouse’s property.
predicates.property_given_for_lifetime_enjoyment: The testamentary disposition gave the spouse a limited right to enjoy the property during the spouse’s lifetime.
predicates.maintenance_purpose_apparent: The disposition and surrounding circumstances show that the property was provided to support the spouse’s maintenance.
predicates.continuous_possession: The spouse continued to possess or enjoy the property under the disposition.

issues.definition: When a testamentary property dispute concerns lifetime enjoyment given to a spouse who had a pre-existing maintenance right, and the grant served that maintenance purpose while the spouse possessed or enjoyed the property, the limited interest becomes absolute.

issues.legal_issue: Specific pleading and proof that a testamentary grant was in lieu of maintenance are unnecessary when the grant and the spouse’s continuing enjoyment of the property for maintenance are undisputed.
material_facts: The genuineness of the will providing the wife with lifetime enjoyment of the property was not disputed.
It was not disputed that the wife continued to enjoy the property by way of maintenance.
The claim that a specific maintenance plea and supporting proof were required was rejected on those undisputed facts.
issues.conclusion: The specific pleading and proof were unnecessary because the bequest and the wife’s continuing enjoyment of the property for maintenance were undisputed; the court’s decision in G. Rama v. T.G. Seshagiri Rao did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Where the bequest in favour of the wife and her continuous possession or enjoyment of the property for maintenance are undisputed, the question of specific pleading and proof on that point does not arise. G. Rama v. T.G. Seshagiri Rao (2008) 12 SCC 392 was inapplicable in those circumstances.

predicates.testamentary_property_dispute: The dispute concerns property given to a spouse under a testamentary disposition.
predicates.bequest_and_continuing_enjoyment_undispu: The parties do not dispute the bequest to the spouse or the spouse’s continued possession or enjoyment of the property.
predicates.maintenance_basis_undisputed: The parties do not dispute that the spouse enjoyed the property for maintenance.

issues.definition: When a testamentary property dispute involves an undisputed bequest, continuing enjoyment, and maintenance basis, specific pleading and proof of the maintenance purpose are not required.
